quiz.q: What did S&P Global do to Poland's credit rating on Nov 6?
options: Upgraded it to A
Kept A- but cut the outlook to negative
Cut it to BBB+
Withdrew the rating
quiz.explain: S&P affirmed A- but moved the outlook from stable to negative, citing deficits above 7% of GDP and presidential vetoes.

quiz.q: How many US nonfarm jobs did the BLS report for October 2026?
quiz.explain: Payrolls rose 165,000, well above forecasts, with unemployment at 4.1%. Markets then priced about an 85% chance of a December Fed hike.

quiz.q: What did the Indian Union Cabinet approve for Agniveers this week?
options: Permanent induction for all
An optional two-year Second Tour of Duty
Scrapping the scheme
A cut in Seva Nidhi
quiz.explain: The Cabinet approved an optional two-year Second Tour of Duty, ahead of the first batch exiting on Nov 21.

lessonQuiz.q: From January, Democrats will hold about 54 Senate seats and more than 250 House seats. What does that mean for bills Trump vetoes?
options: They can override any veto by simple majority
They can override only in the House
They will usually need Republican votes, because two-thirds of both chambers is required
Vetoed bills go automatically to the Supreme Court
lessonQuiz.explain: An override needs 67 senators and 290 representatives if all seats are filled and voting. A narrow majority falls short, so the veto usually holds (Lesson 7).

lessonQuiz.q: Nawrocki appointed new NBP board members only after Tusk countersigned. What does this show about Poland's mixed system?
options: The prime minister can veto any law
Many presidential acts need the prime minister's countersignature, so rivals must sometimes cooperate
The president appoints the whole government alone
The Sejm must approve every presidential decision
lessonQuiz.explain: Countersignature ties the president to the government for many acts. In cohabitation it gives each side leverage, which can produce deals as well as standoffs.

lessonQuiz.q: Why is India's presidential veto described as weaker than Poland's, even though both presidents can return a bill?
options: India's president cannot return any bill
An Indian bill re-passed by an ordinary majority must be signed, while Poland requires three-fifths of the Sejm
Poland's president can dissolve the Sejm after any veto
India requires a referendum to override
lessonQuiz.explain: India's Article 111 veto only delays; Poland's Article 122 veto needs a three-fifths Sejm vote to overcome, which coalition governments often lack.
